block-guide:
CORE/POST-DATE (Date) Draws the publish (or last-modified) date of the current page or post. The date comes from the record; never write a date into the block. Places: a Fabrement template frame (usually a post template, under core/post-title) or a Query's post-template. A Fabrement template replaces the whole page, so the theme's date line is not drawn unless the frame has this block. MARKUP (comment only; no HTML) — the form the editor writes in this WordPress: Last-modified date: the same with "field":"modified". With options: A bare also shows the publish date, but the editor rewrites it to the binding form on the next save; write the binding form. format: a PHP date format ("F j, Y", "d.m.Y"); "human-diff" = "3 days ago"; none = the site's date format (Settings > General). isLink links to the record. Centered text is style.typography.textAlign, as on other blocks. OUTPUT
October 26, 2026
PITFALLS - Pages have dates too: a page template with post-date shows the page's creation date. Keep it for posts unless the user wants it. - The modified date draws nothing until the record is changed after it was published. - Outside a Query on an archive it shows the first listed post's date. CHECK Open an assigned post: its date appears once, in the site's format or the one set.
